The test image shows: stem tissue with **white fluffy mycelial growth** and **black sclerotia** (hard, dark round structures) embedded within bleached/necrotic stem tissue. This is very characteristic.

Top candidates: **White_Mold** (white mycelium + black sclerotia on stem) and possibly Diaporthe (black pycnidia on stems).

Let me view reference images to confirm.

**Analysis of test image:**
- **Affected part:** Stem (lower/mid stem at node area)
- **Key features:** White fluffy mycelial growth on stem surface, multiple black sclerotia (hard, rounded, dark structures ~2-4mm) embedded in and on the bleached/necrotic stem tissue
- **Additional:** Stem tissue appears bleached white, surrounding tissue shows brown necrosis

**Comparison to candidates:**
- **White_Mold**: Perfect match — "black sclerotia embedded within white fluffy mold on stem lesions," "white fluffy mycelial growth on stems especially at nodes," "hard, black sclerotia resembling rodent droppings on or inside stems." The test image shows exactly this.
- **Diaporthe**: Black pycnidia in linear rows — not fluffy white mycelium; ruled out.
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Microsclerotia are tiny and internal, giving a charcoal-sprinkled look; no white fluffy mycelium.
- **Anthracnose**: Dark lesions with setae/acervuli, no white mycelium or sclerotia.

The white fluffy mycelium + prominent black sclerotia on stem is pathognomonic for White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot). This is a definitive visual match.
